$comment: Occupation taxonomy. O*NET-SOC codes as the backbone reference (approximate where a role is emerging and has no clean SOC). Synonyms are matched against cleaned posting titles (lowercased, seniority stripped). Seeded deepest for the launch vertical (architecture); every profession is accepted and mapped from day one. Log unmapped titles, review, extend.

occupations.title: Architect
occupations.desc: Designs buildings and the documents that get them built. Balances program, code, budget, and intent across years-long projects.

license.label: State architecture license (RA/ARB) — registration required to practice/title

occupations.title: Computational Designer
occupations.desc: Turns design intent into code. Writes algorithms and scripts to generate geometry, automate documentation, and solve problems that would be impossible by hand.

occupations.title: BIM Manager
occupations.desc: Owns the digital model across a project team. Sets standards, coordinates disciplines, and makes sure every drawing in the set comes from one source of truth.

occupations.title: Creative Technologist
occupations.desc: Sits between design and engineering. Builds prototypes and interactive experiences for brands, museums, and studios — making technical ideas physical and legible.

occupations.title: Data Analyst
occupations.desc: Turns messy business data into decisions. Runs the queries, builds the dashboards, and translates what patterns actually mean for the people making the calls.

occupations.title: UX Designer
occupations.desc: Designs how software should feel to use. Researches users, maps flows, sketches interfaces, and defends the human experience against every other project pressure.

occupations.title: Product Designer
occupations.desc: Owns a digital product's look, feel, and story end to end. Combines visual design, systems thinking, and close collaboration with engineers and PMs.

occupations.title: Interior Technologist
occupations.desc: Bridges architecture and interior design with the technical detail work. FF&E, materials, specification writing, and coordination with contractors.

occupations.title: Urban Planner
occupations.desc: Shapes cities and neighborhoods over years, not weeks. Works with public policy, GIS data, and community input to design zoning, mobility, and public space.

license.label: State landscape-architecture license in most states
Contractor licensing varies by state; certifications (CCM) common
PE license required to sign/seal structural work
PE license required for responsible charge
PE license required for sign-off roles
CPA license required for public accounting/attest work
FINRA licenses required for securities roles; CFA common
CPA typically required for external audit
State insurance licenses for some lines
State APRN license + national certification required
Certification (CMA/RMA) commonly expected; varies by state
RD/RDN credential + state licensure in most states
State license required for clinical roles (LCSW)
State teaching certification required for public schools
PE required for sign-off roles; not for most product/manufacturing roles
PE required for public-facing/utility sign-off; not for product roles
Code certifications (AWS) required for structural work
FAA certification via the airline required

occupations.title: Architectural Drafter
occupations.desc: Turns an architect's design into the precise drawings a project gets built from. Lives in Revit and AutoCAD; owns the accuracy of the set.

occupations.title: Teaching Assistant
occupations.desc: Supports a classroom teacher and the students who need the most help. The most common way into the education profession.

occupations.title: Building Surveyor
occupations.desc: Inspects buildings for defects, compliance, and condition. Advises on repair, regulation, and value across a building's life.

occupations.title: Maintenance Technician
occupations.desc: Keeps equipment and buildings running. Diagnoses faults, makes repairs, and prevents the breakdowns before they happen.

occupations.title: Police Officer
occupations.desc: Enforces the law and responds to incidents in a community. Public-sector work with clear rank structure and pension.

occupations.title: AI Engineer
occupations.desc: Builds products on top of large language models and machine-learning systems — retrieval pipelines, agents, evaluation, and the engineering that makes AI reliable in production.

occupations.title: MLOps Engineer
occupations.desc: Owns the path from model to production: training pipelines, deployment, monitoring, drift, and the infrastructure that keeps machine learning running.

occupations.title: Prompt Engineer
occupations.desc: Designs, tests, and versions the instructions that steer large language models — prompt systems, evaluation suites, and guardrails for AI products.

occupations.title: Computer Vision Engineer
occupations.desc: Teaches machines to see: detection, segmentation, tracking, and imaging pipelines for products from robotics to medical imaging.

occupations.title: NLP Engineer
occupations.desc: Builds systems that read and write language — classification, extraction, search, and LLM-based applications over text.

occupations.title: Robotics Engineer
occupations.desc: Designs and programs robots — kinematics, control systems, perception, and the integration of hardware with autonomy software.

occupations.title: AI Product Manager
occupations.desc: Product management where the product is a model: scoping AI capabilities, evaluation criteria, data strategy, and shipping ML-powered features responsibly.

occupations.title: Data Architect
occupations.desc: Designs how an organization's data lives: warehouses, lakes, models, governance, and the pipelines between them.
